# Focus patches to gpui 0.2.2

- `src/text_system/line_wrapper.rs`: `LineWrapper::is_word_char` counts the Hebrew and Arabic blocks (U+0590 to U+08FF, U+FB1D to U+FDFF, U+FE70 to U+FEFF) as word characters, so an Arabic word wraps at a space instead of between two letters; Han characters stay breakable between any two.
- `src/text_system/line_layout.rs`: a line that holds right-to-left text and is wider than its wrap width is cut in logical order (`LineLayoutCache::wrap_logically`): advances come from the whole shaped line, break opportunities follow `LineWrapper`, each line is shaped on its own and the lines are laid end to end, so wrap boundaries fall at the first glyph of each line. `compute_wrap_boundaries` walked glyphs in visual order and cut Arabic paragraphs into one letter, then the rest past the edge. Left-to-right text keeps the original path.
- `src/text_system/line.rs`: `paint_line` and `paint_line_background` look up the style run of each glyph by its byte index (`style_run_at`) instead of advancing through the runs: the glyphs of a right-to-left run come in decreasing index order, which shifted colors and dropped backgrounds (inline code in an Arabic paragraph had none). Left-to-right text gets the same runs as before.
- `src/platform/linux/text_system.rs`: the system face "Noto Color Emoji" is removed from the font database (about 38 MiB of heap once an emoji is shaped); an embedded "Noto Emoji" face is registered under that name at every weight from 100 to 900, since cosmic-text falls back to emoji by that name and only at the exact requested weight.
- `src/platform/linux/wayland/client.rs`: the Wayland cursor takes its initial size from `XCURSOR_SIZE` (8 to 256, else 24); it was fixed at 24, and a compositor without the settings portal never corrected it.
- `src/platform/linux/wayland/window.rs`, `src/platform.rs`, `src/window.rs`, `src/platform/linux/wayland/client.rs` (`loop_handle` visible in the crate): no work at rest under Wayland. `frame()` asked a new frame callback at every `done` and `completed_frame` committed every time, so a still window committed and woke the process at the display's rate. Now a frame callback is asked in `draw`, before the renderer presents (its commit carries it), and `completed_frame` commits nothing: a frame that draws nothing ends the loop. `PlatformWindow::frame_waker` (default `None`) gives `WindowInvalidator` a callback that, when the window becomes dirty or `on_next_frame` gets a callback, runs a frame on the next turn of the event loop if no callback is pending. Measured on 2026-11-13 with `tools/tests/idle-frames.sh` (`fixtures/vault`, a note in Read, 10 s after 2 s of rest, 60 Hz output): 600 commits and 600 frame requests, 667 voluntary context switches, 50 ms CPU before; 0, 0, 67 and 30 ms after. With a focused editor (blinking caret): 620 commits before, 20 after. Key to committed image (`tools/tests/key-latency.sh`, 50 keys, reading demo with a Live block): median 15.25 ms before, 3.25 ms after.
- `src/window.rs`, module `ui_profile`: the frame profiler inherited from another project is armed by `FOCUS_UI_PROFILE` (was a variable named after that project) and appends its report every 5 s to `ui-profile.log` in `FOCUS_DATA_DIR`, else `~/.local/share/focus` (was a folder named after that project under `~/.config`). Comments and report in English.
- `src/platform/linux/wayland/window.rs`, configure handler: the interactive resize throttle applies only while a frame callback is pending. Its `done` is what lifts the throttle, and a still window has none since the change above: a resize configure that draws nothing would otherwise drop every later one.
- `src/platform/linux/wayland/window.rs`: two more requests waited for the periodic commit to take effect. A `configure` that resizes nothing (state or decoration change, a size of 0 by 0) now commits its `ack_configure` and window geometry at once; a resize still lets the next drawn frame commit them with its new buffer. `set_background_appearance` commits the opaque region it sets.
- `src/platform/linux/x11/client.rs`: the refresh period comes from the RandR mode of the CRTC under the window's centre, else of the first CRTC with a mode; it came from the first CRTC listed, the wrong one on a machine with two screens at different rates. Compiled, not run (no X11 session here). Still as upstream: the period is not read again when the window moves to another screen, and the refresh timer wakes the process at the display's rate at rest (it draws nothing when nothing is dirty).
- `src/window.rs`: the animation gate inherited with this copy of gpui (`ANIMATION_FRAME_GAP`, 15 ms, `open_animation_gate`) is removed. `request_animation_frame` notifies its view at the next frame of the window, so an animation follows the display's rate (144 or 320 Hz) and stops when it stops asking; the frame callbacks of the compositor pace it under Wayland. Measured on 2026-11-13 at 60 Hz with `tools/tests/idle-frames.sh`: rest 0 commits and caret 19 commits in 10 s, as before; ten palette fades of 100 ms gave frames 21 ms apart (median), the palette's own frame cost limiting them, and none after the last fade closed.
- `src/platform/linux/wayland/window.rs`: a window froze after a fullscreen change under Hyprland on 2026-11-13 (NVIDIA, direct scanout on; not reproduced on a headless output). A frame that drew now commits in `completed_frame`, as upstream did for every frame: blade skips the present of a swapchain that is out of date, and the frame callback asked in `draw` was then never committed, so no `done` came and the window never drew again. The focused window is also drawn when its pending callback is older than 100 ms and something changed, and a configure of the current size commits its ack at once. Cost: a drawn frame takes two commits; a still window still takes none.
- `src/platform/blade/blade_renderer.rs`, `src/platform/linux/wayland/window.rs`: the fullscreen freeze of 2026-11-13 is a swapchain out of date, read in the user's `WAYLAND_DEBUG` log: in fullscreen at 1920 by 1080, 583 frames drawn and committed, 0 buffer attached, the dmabuf feedback with a scanout tranche arriving just after the swapchain was created. `BladeRenderer::draw` now recreates a swapchain found out of date (`Frame::is_valid`, vendored blade-graphics) and acquires again, and returns whether it presented; the Wayland window asks the next frame to present again when it did not.
- `src/platform.rs`, `src/platform/linux/wayland/window.rs`: `set_activation_token` keeps an XDG activation token received from another process; the next `activate` of a Wayland window uses it (`xdg_activation_v1.activate`) instead of asking its own, which a compositor refuses without a fresh user input. Focus hands it over from a second launch (`XDG_ACTIVATION_TOKEN`), so "Open with" from a file manager raises the open window. X11 unchanged (`DESKTOP_STARTUP_ID` is not used).
- `src/platform.rs`, `src/window.rs`, `src/platform/linux/wayland.rs`, `src/platform/linux/wayland/client.rs`, `src/platform/linux/wayland/window.rs`, `src/platform/linux/wayland/clipboard.rs`, `src/platform/linux/wayland/drag_out.rs` (new): `Window::start_data_drag` hands the drag the left button holds to the compositor as a Wayland drag source (`wl_data_device.start_drag`, serial of the press), offering the given types for copying only, so a note dragged out of the file tree reaches another application (docs/SPEC.md, Files). `PlatformWindow::start_data_drag` returns `false` elsewhere (X11 included). `wl_data_source.send` serves the drag's bodies (`Clipboard::send_internal`, now `pub(crate)`), the clipboard's otherwise. When the compositor ends the drag (`dnd_finished`, `cancelled`), the window's own drag gets a mouse up away from every element, since the button release no longer reaches it. Back over one of our windows, the offer is accepted with a private type only (`application/x-focus-drag`) and its motion and drop become mouse moves and a mouse up: the window's drag goes on, and a drop there is never read as files from outside. Decisions in `drag_out.rs`, tested from `crates/focus-view-vault` (`#[path]`). Not run against a compositor by a test: the capture scripts cannot press a real button.
- `src/text_system/line_caret.rs` (new), `src/text_system/line_layout.rs`, `src/text_system.rs`: the caret and hit tests of right-to-left text. `LineLayout::x_for_index` returned the x of the first glyph, in visual order, whose index reached the one asked; in a right-to-left run the glyphs come in decreasing index order, so every index of the run got the x of its leftmost glyph, and a wrapped right-to-left line (laid out end to end, `wrap_logically`) took the index of its leftmost glyph as its first byte. Each visual line is now its glyphs, its edges and its bytes (`CaretLine`, `WrappedLineLayout::caret_lines`, bytes from the smallest index of its glyphs); the caret before a character of a right-to-left run sits on its right edge, a character reads right to left when a visual neighbour is its logical neighbour on the other side (alone between two of the other direction it counts as left to right), and the closest boundary to an x is the near edge of the glyph under it in that direction. `x_for_index`, `closest_index_for_x`, `WrappedLineLayout::position_for_index` and `index_for_position` use them; left-to-right text gets the positions it had. The source editor of gpui-component goes through the same functions. Tests: `crates/focus-view-reading/src/text.rs`, module `caret_tests` (this crate is not a workspace member), and the Arabic case of `tools/tests/inplace-text.sh`.
- `src/elements/text.rs`: `TextLayout` keeps the `text_align` it was laid out with, and `position_for_index` and `index_for_position` shift each visual line as `paint` aligns it in the element's width (`CaretLine::aligned_left`, the formula of `aligned_origin_x`); they started every line at the left edge, so on a short right-aligned line (Arabic in Read) a selection and a click landed beside the text. `TextLayout::closest_index_for_position` gives the character boundary nearest a point, where a caret goes (editing in place, `crates/focus-view-reading`).
- `build.rs`, `src/platform/windows/directx_renderer.rs`: a Windows build made on Linux (cargo-xwin, `aarch64-pc-windows-msvc`). The module that compiles the HLSL shaders with `fxc.exe` and embeds the manifest exists only when the build itself runs on Windows, so such a release had neither its shaders (`shaders_bytes.rs` missing) nor its manifest (per monitor DPI awareness, common controls 6 that `TaskDialogIndirect` needs). On another host, `build.rs` now writes the two shader files to `OUT_DIR` with `alpha_correction.hlsl` inlined and sets `gpui_shaders_at_launch`: each shader is compiled at launch from that text by `D3DCompile` (d3dcompiler_47.dll of Windows, optimization level 3 in release). The manifest is compiled by `llvm-rc` (or `$RC`) into `gpui_manifest.lib`, linked as embed-resource links a library's resource. A build on Windows is unchanged. Not run on Windows yet: the time the shaders take at launch is not measured.
- `src/window.rs`: `DispatchEventResult` is public, as the `Window::dispatch_event` that returns it already was: the capture scripts press the pointer through it (`mouse <x> <y>`, `pick <row>`), which runs the focus transfer of a real press.
- `src/style.rs`, `src/styled.rs`, `src/text_system.rs`, `src/text_system/line_layout.rs`, `src/text_system/line_wrapper.rs`, `src/elements/text.rs`: letter spacing (DESIGN 3 tracking of the Sora styles). `TextStyle::letter_spacing` (pixels, cascades, `Styled::letter_spacing`) is a property of a shaped line, as the font size is. `LineLayout::apply_letter_spacing` moves the glyphs once the platform has shaped the line, in the platform independent layer, so Linux and Windows get it alike: in screen order, the spacing is added between two neighbouring characters, never between the glyphs of one character, never after the last one, and never beside a right-to-left character (no tracking on Arabic, as CSS leaves cursive scripts alone); the width changes by the sum. The value is part of the key of `LineLayoutCache` and goes through `wrap_logically`, so every number read from a layout (width, wrap boundaries, `x_for_index`, `closest_index_for_x`, `index_for_x`, the caret lines of `line_caret.rs`, selection and match rectangles, decorations) comes from the moved glyphs. `WindowTextSystem::shape_text_spaced` and `shape_line_spaced`, `TextSystem::line_wrapper_spaced` take the spacing; `shape_text`, `shape_line`, `layout_line` and `line_wrapper` keep their upstream signatures with no spacing, so gpui-component and the other callers are unchanged. `TextLayout` (the text of a `div`, `StyledText`) shapes with the spacing of its text style and truncates with a spaced `LineWrapper`, which adds the spacing between two characters as shaping does (`truncate_line`, and `wrap_line` including the candidate width and the hanging indent). `LineLayout::compute_wrap_boundaries` is public and `GlyphId` has `From<u32>`, for the tests: `crates/focus-kit/src/typography.rs`, module `text_layout_tests` (width, x for an index, index for an x, wrap boundary and caret positions with and without tracking, Arabic, mixed text, a base and its mark). Still approximate as upstream: `LineWrapper` measures characters one by one, without kerning, so a truncation point can differ from the shaped line by the kerning of a pair.
- `src/platform/linux/text_system.rs`, `src/platform/linux/font_weight.rs` (new): cosmic-text takes a script fallback family only at the exact requested weight, so a Sora 600 title in Chinese skipped Noto Sans CJK SC (no 600 face) and fell on a serif CJK face, a Noto Serif CJK SemiBold. `offer_fallbacks_at_every_weight` gives Noto Sans CJK SC and the embedded Noto Sans Arabic a face at every weight from 100 to 900, the face CSS font matching picks for it (`nearest_weight`: 600 takes Bold, Arabic 700 takes SemiBold), at start and after `add_fonts`; Source Han Sans SC answers under the name Noto Sans CJK SC when the latter is missing (DESIGN 10: Noto Sans CJK SC, then Source Han Sans SC, then the system CJK font). The order of the script fallbacks stays cosmic-text's: under a Japanese, Korean or traditional Chinese locale Han goes to Noto Sans CJK JP, KR, TC or HK first. Windows (DirectWrite) is unchanged: its system fallback already picks a sans CJK face, and `Font::fallbacks` is not set by the application. Tests: `crates/focus-kit/src/fonts.rs`, module `fallback_tests` (`#[path]`).
- `src/elements/text.rs`: a `TextLayout` with a text overflow (`text_ellipsis`, `truncate`) and no wrapping kept the size of its first measure: taffy measures a flex item at its max-content width first, so the text was never cut and only clipped by its parent (the latest events of the Ops dashboard, docs/SPEC.md). Such a text is laid out again at each measure; shaping stays cached by `LineLayoutCache`.
- `src/text_system/line_wrapper.rs`, `src/text_system/line_layout.rs`: a line never starts with closing punctuation nor ends with opening punctuation. Every character but a word character after a space was a break opportunity, so a line of a note could start with ", tags" (the comma after inline code, whose directional isolate U+2069 counted as a breakable character). `LineBreaks` (public) reads a line character after character and gives its break opportunities: as before, before a word that follows a space and before any other character but a space (CJK breaks between two characters), but never before closing punctuation (`, . ; : ! ?`, closing brackets and quotes, the ellipsis, the CJK closing marks and the Arabic comma, semicolon and question mark), never after opening punctuation (opening brackets and quotes, `¿ ¡`, the CJK opening brackets), and a run of format characters (directional marks and isolates, joiners) breaks with the character after it. An ASCII `"` opens after a space, the start of the line or an opening mark, and closes otherwise. `LineWrapper::wrap_line`, `LineLayout::compute_wrap_boundaries` (read once per character, not per glyph, so a base and its marks no longer make a CJK break between them) and `LineLayoutCache::wrap_logically` all use it. Tests: `crates/focus-kit/src/typography.rs`, module `text_layout_tests`.
- `src/elements/div.rs`: `TOOLTIP_SHOW_DELAY` is 400 ms instead of 500 ms, the tooltip delay of docs/DESIGN.md section 7.
- `src/window.rs`, `src/interactive.rs`, `src/platform.rs`: a zoom of the window, for the interface size setting of the application (`appearance.ui_scale`, 90 to 120 %, and its keys). `Window::set_zoom(z)` and `Window::zoom()`; the window draws with the platform's scale factor times `z` and lays out in a viewport of the content size divided by `z` (`Window::new` starts at 1, `bounds_changed` applies it), so every pixel of the layout covers `z` pixels and text is rasterized at the zoomed scale, not stretched. Positions from the platform are divided by `z` where platform input enters (`PlatformInput::unzoomed`, in the `on_input` closure: pointer down, up, move, exit, the wheel's position and pixel delta, file drag positions), not in `Window::dispatch_event`, which the capture scripts call with positions of the zoomed layout; the pointer position kept by the window is converted when the zoom changes. Positions given to the platform are multiplied by `z`: the IME position (`invalidate_character_coordinates`, `PlatformInputHandler::bounds_for_range`), the window menu position, the client inset, `Window::resize`; `PlatformInputHandler::character_index_for_point` divides its point. `Window::bounds`, `window_bounds` and `inner_window_bounds` stay in the platform's coordinates (screen placement). `paint_quad` rounds border widths to whole device pixels, at least one, so a 1 px rule stays one device pixel at a fractional scale; at integer scales the widths are unchanged.
- `src/window.rs`, `paint_underline`: a straight underline is a whole number of device pixels thick, at least one, and starts on a device pixel row, as `paint_quad` rounds border widths since the window zoom: at 110 or 120 % a 1 px link or search match underline was 1.1 or 1.2 device pixels spread over two rows. Wavy underlines are unchanged.
